sub_scenario.family: APAC verbal ownership under incomplete records
sub_scenario.one_line: radiology workflow coordinator: carry the symptom, concern, and pending-result labels into the bridge

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the radiology workflow coordinator and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The imaging queue review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can read the completed imaging queue to the next shift.
Does that involve uncertainty?
No, completed studies are already signed off.
Someone new shadowed me in the APAC bridge this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the urgent-study handoff into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
For an urgent neuroimaging request, I send a written triage note that labels confirmed symptoms, the referring clinician's concern, and missing contraindication details.
Why label the sources?
So the incoming coordinator does not mistake a concern for a cleared indication.
I can book a scanner slot after a radiologist approves it.
Can booking alone determine priority?
No, the clinical rationale comes first.
I archived last cycle's notes on the imaging queue and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The 06:55 Tokyo bridge is followed by a scanner-maintenance lock at 07:20.
Why does that matter?
The urgent slot must be protected before the lock begins.
A vendor call about the radiology workflow coordinator ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the APAC bridge checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the urgent-study handoff.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the imaging queue records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
I once verbally described a patient as cleared for contrast when the renal result was still pending, and the slot had to be cancelled at the door.
What caused the cancellation?
I collapsed a pending result into a definite clearance.
I sketched next week's plan for the urgent-study handoff before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the radiology workflow coordinator updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The night team decorates the control room with paper cranes during festival week.
Does that change triage?
No, it is only part of the room's atmosphere.
A senior physician says taking the handoff will show that I can keep the queue moving.
Does speed establish clearance?
No, the missing result still needs to be visible.
I closed the week by updating the APAC bridge handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
How should I rank taking the Tokyo urgent-study handoff?
